I need to build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model fine-tuning and alignment. Please access our academic paper repository and read the full content of papers that are relevant to the topics of LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. For each relevant paper, read through its sections carefully to understand the methodology and key results. Skip any papers that are about unrelated topics like robotics or physical systems.

Create a Notion page titled LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each relevant paper, where each block covers the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings from the paper.

Also create a Word document called LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx in my workspace. The document should start with a heading called LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey, followed by an introduction paragraph. Then include a dedicated section for each relevant paper that presents the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections.

Finally, create a Google Sheet called LLM Paper Registry with columns for ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, and Method_Category, with one row per relevant paper.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself runs the compact discovery queries, then uses one parallel full-text reader wave of three per-paper explorers and one parallel writer wave of three deliverable owners.

Before Wave 1, the main agent covers the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space in read-only mode through complementary fine-tuning, alignment, and architecture queries at the supported per-call bound; unions and deduplicates all returned IDs (the search exposes no cursor); applies the task's relevance rule (reject robotics or physical-system distractors); and freezes exactly three retained paper IDs — never importing outside facts or importing rejected IDs downstream.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per retained paper ID:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Reader for retained paper 1. Use the local repository read_paper tool with paper_id = that literal assigned ID, read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results, and return EXACTLY the structured report {paper_id, title, full authors, published date, key method, source-backed findings, method category, section coverage}. Read-only: do not create Notion, Word, Google Sheet, or intermediate files.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Reader for retained paper 2 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Reader for retained paper 3 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies one handoff per retained ID, deduplicates titles, verifies every rejected paper against the exclusion rule, and freezes one normalized packet with per-paper controls.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base, create at most one page, add one substantive block per frozen paper with title, method, and findings, and read it back. Return page ID/title, paper coverage, block count, and validation. Do not write the Word document or Google Sheet.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx exclusively. Create it exactly once with the required heading, introduction, and one author/method/results section for every frozen paper. Read it back and return path, headings, retained-paper coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or Google Sheets.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Google Sheet LLM Paper Registry exclusively. Create it once with the exact six columns and one row per frozen paper, preserving full authors and source dates and using controlled Method_Category values. Read it back and return spreadsheet/sheet IDs, headers, row count, and validation. Do not write Notion or Word state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile the same stable-ID set, authors, methods, and findings across all deliverables, verify every rejected paper appears nowhere, and complete only after file and external-state checks. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

nodes.text:
You are planning a multi-system task. Decompose it into ordered, executable subtasks and return a detailed plan.

TASK DESCRIPTION (from the user):
1. Build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model (LLM) fine-tuning and alignment.
2. Access the academic paper repository (MCP tools available: mcp__arxiv_local__* for a local arXiv paper store, and mcp__arxiv-latex__* for arXiv LaTeX access) and read the FULL content of papers relevant to: LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements.
3. For each relevant paper, read sections carefully to understand methodology and key results.
4. SKIP papers about unrelated topics (e.g., robotics, physical systems).
5. Create a Notion page titled "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base". The page must contain blocks for each relevant paper: paper title, key method introduced, main findings.
6. Create a Word document "LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx" in the workspace (workspace root: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace). Structure: a heading "LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey", an introduction paragraph, then a dedicated section per paper containing: paper title, author names, description of the method, key results (extracted from reading the paper sections).
7. Create a Google Sheet called "LLM Paper Registry" with columns: ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, Method_Category — one row per relevant paper.

PLAN REQUIREMENTS:
For each subtask, specify:
- Dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore, or coder.
- Whether the subtask is independent (parallelizable) or depends on another subtask's output.

Your plan should cover, in order:
1. Discovery phase: how to find relevant papers in the local repository (e.g., mcp__arxiv_local__list_papers, mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers) — decide whether to use an explore sub-agent to enumerate candidates and read paper metadata.
2. Reading phase: how to read full paper content (mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper and/or mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt / list_paper_sections / get_paper_section) and how to decide relevance (include LLM fine-tuning/alignment/architecture; exclude robotics/physical systems). Consider that papers may need section-level reading to extract method + key results.
3. Synthesis phase: what information must be extracted per paper (title, authors, published date, arXiv ID, key contribution/method, method category, main findings) to feed all three deliverables.
4. Notion page creation: blocks per paper (title, key method, main findings). Consider using a coder sub-agent to build the page content and create it via Notion API tools.
5. Word document creation: heading, intro paragraph, per-paper sections. Consider using a coder sub-agent with the word MCP tools.
6. Google Sheet creation: create spreadsheet, set columns, one row per paper. Consider using a coder sub-agent with the google_sheet MCP tools.
7. Verification phase: verify each deliverable exists and contains the required content.

Note: the three output deliverables (Notion, Word, Google Sheet) are independent of each other once the per-paper extracted data is ready, so they can be parallelized. The extraction/synthesis of paper data is a prerequisite for all three.

Also note the workspace root where the Word doc must be created, and that sub-agents share the same workspace.

Return: an ordered subtask list with dispatch decision and dependency/parallelism annotations per subtask, plus a verification checklist.
Plan LLM knowledge base task

You are a read-only research assistant extracting detailed content from an arXiv paper for a knowledge base about LLM fine-tuning and alignment. The paper to read is arXiv ID: 2305.20050.

BACKGROUND: The local repo (mcp__arxiv_local__) has 4 papers; this one was pre-classified as RELEVANT to LLM fine-tuning / alignment / model architecture. Your job is to read its full content and extract structured details. NOTE from prior probes: mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper may return empty content in this environment; mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt(arxiv_id) (flattened LaTeX of the full paper) is the reliable full-content source. mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section may return empty for some section paths — try it but don't rely on it.

READING INSTRUCTIONS (use these tools, all read-only):
1. Try mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper with paper_id = 2305.20050 — if it returns substantial content, use it as the primary source.
2. If empty/failed, call mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt(arxiv_id=2305.20050) to get the flattened LaTeX of the whole paper. This is likely your main source — read it thoroughly.
3. Call mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_abstract(arxiv_id=2305.20050) to confirm the abstract and metadata.
4. Optionally try mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections(arxiv_id=2305.20050) then mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section for Introduction/Method/Experiments/Results sections if available, to pin down where key content lives.

READ THE SECTIONS CAREFULLY: go through the introduction, method/approach, experiments, and results sections (or the equivalent structure in the flattened LaTeX) to understand the methodology and the key results.

EXTRACTION SCHEMA — return exactly this structure in your final report:
- arxiv_id: 2305.20050
- title: (exact title from the paper)
- authors: (FULL author list — from the LaTeX \author{} block or metadata; list ALL authors, not just the first two)
- published_date: (date from metadata if present; else infer from arXiv ID YYMM, e.g., 2305 → 2023-05, and state it is inferred)
- abstract: (full abstract text)
- method_category: one of these three labels — "Preference Optimization / RLHF alternative" (if the paper's core contribution is a preference/alignment optimization method), "Fine-tuning & RLHF alignment" (if it is about fine-tuning models or RLHF alignment pipelines), or "Model architecture improvement" (if it is about architecture/efficiency innovations).
- key_method (the key method introduced, 2-4 sentences, from the method sections):
- key_contribution (one concise sentence on the main contribution):
- main_findings / key_results (3-6 bullet points with concrete numbers/benchmarks from the results sections, e.g., win rates, benchmark scores, efficiency gains):
- section_references (which sections contained the method and results, e.g., "Method in §2/§3, Results in §4/§5"):
- relevance_confirmation: confirm this paper is genuinely about LLM fine-tuning / alignment / model architecture (if during reading it turns out to be off-topic such as robotics or physical systems, say EXCLUDE and explain why).

Be thorough and factual — extract real numbers and technical details from the paper content. Do NOT invent content. If a tool returns empty, report which tool failed and continue with the others.
Read 3 relevant arXiv papers

You are a read-only research assistant. Use your browser navigation tools to visit the official arXiv abstract pages for 3 papers and extract precise metadata. These pages are public and contain the full abstract, complete author list, and submission/publication dates.

PAPERS TO FETCH (visit each URL):
1. https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050 (Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model)
2. https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09288 (Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models)
3. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825 (Mistral 7B)

For each paper, extract EXACTLY the following from the page:
- arxiv_id
- full_title (exact title as shown on the page)
- full_abstract (the COMPLETE abstract text, not truncated — copy it fully)
- authors: the COMPLETE author list (all authors, in order, exactly as displayed)
- published_date: the date shown on the page (e.g., "[Submitted on ... ]" / "v1" date; if a specific date is shown, use it; otherwise state the month/year)
- comments: any comments line shown (e.g., number of pages, version info)
- subjects: the arXiv subject categories shown (e.g., cs.CL, cs.LG)

Use browser_navigate to open each page, wait for it to load (browser_wait_for or check page content), and read the visible text. If browser navigation fails for a URL, report the failure and try the alternate URL format (e.g., https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050v1 or the export citation page https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050?context=cs). Do NOT fabricate any data — only report what you actually see on the pages.

Return your findings as a structured list: one block per paper with the fields above filled in. If a field cannot be retrieved, say "NOT RETRIEVED" for it.
Fetch arXiv page metadata

You are a coder sub-agent. Your job: create a Notion page titled "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base" with content blocks for 3 relevant papers.

CONTEXT: A shared dataset exists at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace/papers_dataset.json — read it with mcp__local__python_execute or a local read tool. It contains "survey_title", "intro", and a "papers" list. Each paper has: arxiv_id, title, authors, published_date, method_category, abstract, key_method, key_contribution, main_findings (list).

TASK:
1. Find an appropriate parent for the new page:
   - Call mcp__notion__API-post-search (empty query) to list existing pages/databases. Pick the first top-level page result as the parent (page_id). If none exists, call mcp__notion__API-get-self to confirm the bot, then create the page with parent = the first searchable page; if truly no parent is available, report the blocker.
2. Create the page via mcp__notion__API-post-page with:
   - parent: {"page_id": "<parent page id>"}
   - properties: {"title": {"title": [{"text": {"content": "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base"}}]}} (or the simplified legacy title array form your tool accepts)
   - children: content blocks as described below.
3. Page content structure (children blocks). For EACH of the 3 papers in dataset order, add:
   - a heading_2 block with the paper title
   - a paragraph block: "Key method: " + paper["key_method"]
   - a paragraph block: "Main findings: " + "; ".join(paper["main_findings"])
   - Optionally a bulleted_list_item with the arXiv ID + method category.
   Keep the blocks in the same order as the papers list. Use proper Notion block JSON: e.g. {"type": "heading_2", "heading_2": {"rich_text": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "<title>"}}]}} and {"type": "paragraph", "paragraph": {"rich_text": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "<text>"}}]}}.
4. If API-post-page rejects the children payload (size/validation), create the page with just the title first, then append blocks with mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children (block_id = new page id).
5. Record the new page_id.

RETURN: the new page_id, the parent page used, and a confirmation that the page contains blocks for exactly these 3 papers (arXiv IDs 2305.20050, 2307.09288, 2310.06825) with title/key method/main findings each. If any Notion tool fails, report exactly which call failed and what it returned; do not silently work around infrastructure failures.
Create Notion knowledge base page

Create the document: mcp__word__create_document with filename = the absolute path above (or relative filename if the tool resolves to the workspace; verify with mcp__word__list_available_documents to see how filenames resolve — the workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-review-notion-word/workspace).
